comments.author: @richardadonnell
comments.text:
Hi Wes,

I hope you’re doing well. I wanted to take a moment to share some honest feedback, even though I know it likely won’t reach you or make any difference. I really do appreciate the content you put out—it’s clear you put a lot of thought into it, and it’s one of the reasons I’ve been a loyal viewer.

There are plenty of other YouTubers covering AI-related news, but what sets your channel apart is that your content feels completely different from the overhyped “mainstream” channels. While others tend to chase the latest shiny new tool or software, you have a rare ability to step back and look at the bigger picture—examining the AI industry as a whole from a 10,000-foot view. This perspective is unique and refreshing, and it’s why I keep coming back to your channel.

That said, I—and many others—find the frequent use of words like “shocked” or “shocking” in your titles frustrating. The content rarely aligns with the level of surprise those words suggest, and it’s beginning to feel like clickbait. While I understand the need to attract clicks, this pattern is starting to have the opposite effect.

It’s becoming a bit like "the boy who cried wolf"—if every small piece of news is framed as “shocking,” the term loses its meaning. My concern is that when the day comes where genuinely shocking news breaks, many viewers won’t take it seriously because the term has been diluted by overuse.

You’ve built something special with your channel. The quality of your insights alone is enough to keep viewers coming back—you don’t need to rely on tactics that might yield short-term gains but erode trust with your core audience over time.

I say all this because I value your work and want to see your channel continue to thrive. Thanks for your time reading this, if you do.

Best,
rad
